title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
summary: Fixes a Logcat panel bug that could make VS Code as a whole feel sluggish during or after a debugging session, and makes Stop actually stop the stream.

highlights.title: Logcat Buffer Rewrite
highlights.description: The Logcat webview's mirror buffer used an O(n) eviction on every incoming line once full. Replaced with the same O(1) ring buffer already used on the extension host side.

highlights.title: Stop Now Really Stops
highlights.description: kotlinJump.logcat.stop only muted the panel before; the adb process kept running in the background. Stop now tears the stream down, and the status bar shows a distinct Stopped state.

highlights.title: Lazy ADB Watcher
highlights.description: The ADB device watcher no longer starts at extension activation for every workspace with a Kotlin file. It starts on first use: opening the panel, running a Logcat command, or a successful Android Run.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: Fixed the Logcat webview's mirror buffer, which evicted rows with Array.shift(), an O(n) operation per row that ran on every incoming log line once the buffer filled. Replaced with the ring buffer already used on the extension host side.
Fixed the webview's tag/search/level filter to update incrementally instead of rescanning the entire buffer on every batch of incoming lines.

Fixed kotlinJump.logcat.stop, which only muted forwarding to the panel without stopping the underlying adb logcat process; the stream, parsing, and stack-trace resolution kept running after a Stop. Stop now tears the stream down for real.

The ADB device watcher no longer starts unconditionally at extension activation. It starts lazily on first real use, so a Kotlin file no longer implies an always-on adb process for non-Android workspaces.
The webview no longer keeps re-filtering and re-rendering while the Logcat panel is hidden; it resyncs in one pass when the panel becomes visible again.
